title: Learn to Speak in Headlines
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that senior audiences want orientation before detail, and that leaders who communicate like subject-matter experts rather than as leaders often bury their real message under facts. It recommends opening any presentation or discussion with a single, memorable headline statement before diving into supporting detail, since audiences can't judge what details matter until they know the main point. The piece offers a practical drill, distilling any message, presentation, or piece of content into one or two sentences, as a way for leaders to build this skill deliberately.
points: Senior audiences want orientation and a headline before details, not a comprehensive download.
Leaders who function like experts often bury their real message under excessive detail.
A recommended drill: condense any message or presentation into one or two memorable sentences first.
Practicing headline-writing on others' content is suggested as a way to build the skill.
quotes: The more senior the audience, the more important it is to speak in headlines.
What senior audiences want is the lay of the land, not a topographical map.
Starting with strategic headlines before diving into any topic or issue is how leaders talk to leaders.
Experts love to overwhelm people with the facts and details they know because it displays their deep understanding and knowledge.
People don’t read the copy before they read the headline for a simple reason: They have no idea why the copy matters without a summarizing statement.
